issues.legal_issue: A payment to acquire a long-term right to extract minerals still embedded in land is capital expenditure rather than revenue expenditure.
material_facts: The assessee claimed a deduction for the balance of the amount paid under a lease of mining areas for twenty years.
The areas had previously been worked, and mica pillars had been exposed, but the mica remained embedded in the land and further mining operations were needed to extract it.
A separate amount paid for mica scrap already lying on the surface was allowed as revenue expenditure by the Tribunal; the disputed lease payment related to the right to extract the remaining mica.
issues.conclusion: The disputed lease expenditure was capital expenditure and was not allowable as revenue expenditure.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(xv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, expenditure for acquiring an enduring right over land to win minerals embedded in it is capital expenditure; the need for mining operations to extract the minerals distinguishes it from acquiring surface minerals as stock-in-trade. The Court followed Pingle Industries Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax and applied the fact-specific approach discussed in Atherton v. British Insulated and Helsby Cables Ltd. and Abdul Kayoom v. Commissioner of Income-tax. It also referred to Golden Horse Shoe (New) Ltd. v. Thurgood, Mohanlal Hargovind v. C.I.T., and M.A. Jabbar v. Commissioner of Income-tax in distinguishing minerals already obtained or lying on the surface.

rule.if: income_tax_deduction_claim and mining_lease_acquired and long_term_right_to_extract and mineral_embedded_in_land and extraction_operations_required

predicates.income_tax_deduction_claim: A taxpayer claimed that an expense incurred in its business was deductible in computing income.
predicates.mining_lease_acquired: The taxpayer obtained a lease conferring rights to work a mineral deposit.
predicates.long_term_right_to_extract: The lease conferred a right to extract minerals over an extended period.
predicates.mineral_embedded_in_land: The minerals covered by the disputed payment remained embedded in the land rather than already being obtained and lying on the surface.
predicates.extraction_operations_required: The taxpayer had to perform mining operations to extract the minerals.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer claims a deduction for a mining-lease payment and the lease gives an extended right to extract minerals that remain embedded in land through mining operations, the payment is treated as capital expenditure.

issues.legal_issue: A fee paid for a prospecting licence to search for minerals and initiate a mining business is capital expenditure rather than revenue expenditure.
material_facts: The assessee claimed a deduction for a fee paid to obtain a prospecting licence.
The fee was payable per acre and did not depend on the quantity of minerals obtained.
The licence permitted investigation and search for minerals, which had to be won and extracted from the earth; the authorities found that the payment was to initiate mining operations.
The licence was for one year, but the Court held that this duration did not make the payment revenue expenditure.
issues.conclusion: The prospecting licence fee was capital expenditure and was not allowable as revenue expenditure.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(2)(xv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, does not allow a prospecting fee as revenue expenditure where its object is to initiate the business of extracting minerals from the earth. A fee unrelated to the quantity of minerals obtained and paid for the right to investigate, search for, and find minerals is not a payment to acquire stock-in-trade; the short duration of the licence does not alter its character. The Court applied its capital-versus-revenue analysis, including the principles discussed in Pingle Industries Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax.

rule.if: income_tax_deduction_claim and prospecting_license_obtained and license_for_mineral_search and minerals_require_extraction_from_earth and fee_independent_of_mineral_quantity

predicates.income_tax_deduction_claim: A taxpayer claimed that an expense incurred in its business was deductible in computing income.
predicates.prospecting_license_obtained: The taxpayer obtained a licence to prospect for minerals.
predicates.license_for_mineral_search: The licence permitted investigation and search to locate minerals for a proposed extraction business.
predicates.minerals_require_extraction_from_earth: The minerals sought under the licence had to be won and extracted from the earth.
predicates.fee_independent_of_mineral_quantity: The fee was payable without reference to the quantity of minerals obtained.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer claims a deduction for a fee paid for a mineral-search licence and the fee is independent of output while the minerals must be extracted from the earth, the fee is treated as capital expenditure.
